cells.A3: 22 OCT CORRECTIONS (critical review, founder's choices): a 10% contingency on the cost to win a saver; tech ₹4 a month per KYC'd user reached (savers and the KYC'd users who came with them), not ₹1 per saver; payments ₹2 a debit, weekly debits until BSE StAR MF confirms a daily SIP on one mandate; insurance a fixed referral fee, not counted (0); Choti, gold and other products not counted; 70% of gold-loan applications approved; the non-savers see gold, property and home loans only. Each is an input on v4 Inputs. Every figure here is a plan with targets, not evidence.
cells.A4: LOAN MARKETPLACE (operator 21 Oct): loan offers go to anyone KYC'd who opts in, from day 1 (2.5 KYC'd users per online saver won: 5 sign-ups, half finish KYC), reachable as long as savers keep saving; 35% apply for a loan a year (70% personal or business, 15% gold, 3% property, 2% home; 35% is a target, inside which the opt-in sits); 30% of first applications approved, 70% of repeats; DSA payouts (2% on personal and business loans, rising to 3% by year 5). v4 Monthly 'loans to KYC'd users who never save' adds the non-savers' loans to revenue; the input is at the end of v4 Inputs. v4 LTV shows one saver's waterfall live.
cells.A5: The OLDER tabs (Inputs, Per saver, Monthly, Summary, Assumptions, Monte Carlo, Sign-ups, Agent pay, Sensitivity and the Company / City tabs) are the SUPERSEDED street-fleet model of 16-18 Oct. They are HIDDEN since 22 Oct (View > Hidden sheets to see them); do not use them for the plan. No v4 formula reads them, and no v4 name clashes with theirs (every v4 name starts with v_).

cells.A10: 3. 'v4 Summary' puts the live answer next to the Python model's 22 Oct run at 20,000 and 1,50,000 a month (fixed values). Column E picks the Python value at your plan level (growth 1.0); the gap is meaningful while the other inputs are at their 22 Oct values.
cells.A11: 4. To try a lever (v4 Levers), type the inputs in its last column into v4 Inputs; the sheet reproduces each lever.
cells.A14: v4 Inputs: every input with its value, unit and source (blue), the worked-out values (grey) and the 19 cross-sell products.
cells.A15: v4 Per saver: one saver's months 1-96. For the online and the doorstep saver: still saving, deposits, balance, fund trail, loan fees, cards, insurance, other products, serving (support, tech, payments) and cumulative revenue less serving. To the right, the machinery shared by both savers (per active saver): the fund balance, the loan states, top-ups, cards and every product's take-ups and money.
cells.A16: v4 Monthly: months 1-96: savers won (online path, pool cap, doorstep agents and their ramp), active savers, AUM, revenue by line, acquisition, the team by role, other costs, EBITDA, tax after losses carried forward, PAT, cumulative cash, the two lenses and each product's money.
cells.A17: v4 Yearly: years 1-8 (SUMIFS on Monthly), ₹ crore.
cells.A18: v4 Summary: the headline measures, live, next to the Python run; the reconciliation table.
cells.A19: v4 Levers, v4 Monte Carlo: pasted values from the Python model (tables/online_levers.csv, online_frontier.csv, online_mc_summary.csv, online_mc_drivers.csv, online_mc_inputs.csv), run 22 Oct 2026. They do not move.
cells.A22: Per active saver: every line except 'still saving' is the same for the online and the doorstep saver (take-ups, loan states and cross-sell all scale with still saving in the Python engine), so Per saver works it once, and each saver's lines are the still-saving curve x those per-active lines.
cells.A23: Cohorts: each Monthly line = the sum over every month's savers won of (still saving at their age x the per-active line at that age): one MMULT of a 96 x 96 matrix (month x age) per line, online and doorstep savers together.
cells.A24: Products: each of the 19 products is worked in closed form: take-ups = never-held x the monthly hazard (early factor in the saver's months 1-6; home loans and LAP x approval), money = take-ups x the kind's rule (commission at take-up, renewals each year, the Choti bonus at month 24, monthly holdings for gold, recharge and bills).
cells.A26: Simplifications (each measured against the Python model; model/v4_toy_check.py)
cells.A27: 1. Calendar growth. In Python, take-up grows 5% and approval 10% each calendar year (held after year 5) and every month's cohort has its own profile. The sheet computes one profile at the held year (exact for every cohort from month 49) and scales each month by that month's factor relative to the held year: take-up for insurance and other products, take-up x approval for loan fees, cards, home loans and LAP.
cells.A28: 2. Timing of the later money: money booked at take-up takes this month's factor; insurance renewals the factor of 12 months earlier, the Choti bonus 24 months earlier, holdings (gold, recharge, bills) 6 months earlier (lag_hold, a sheet-only calibration: holdings build from take-ups spread over their life, and the never-held pool offsets part of the lag; 0 = this month's factor, 6 tracks the Python model best).
cells.A29: 3. Loan fees take the take-up x approval factor of the month for first loans, repeats and top-ups alike.
cells.A30: 4. Fixed in the sheet as in the Python plan: the marketplace opens in the saver's month 1; early factors in months 1-6; a stopper lapses their policies and holdings; no interest on cash.
cells.A31: Costs and cash, exactly as the Python plan: a 10% contingency on every expensed line inside EBITDA (contingency); revenue booked when earned but its cash 2 months later (comm_lag), so cash flow = PAT - revenue + cash received; money needed = the deepest cumulative cash hole + ₹5 crore. Both are blue inputs on v4 Inputs.
cells.A33: Reconciliation at the 22 Oct inputs (full table on v4 Summary and tables/v4_toy_check.csv)
cells.A34: Revenue within 1.01% in every year at both levels. EBITDA year 5: 7.728 vs 7.798 ₹ crore at 20,000 a month (-0.90%); 69.168 vs 69.796 at 1,50,000 (-0.90%); year 8 +0.21% and +0.17%. EBITDA positive from month 49 and 48 (Python 49 and 48). Money needed +0.70% and +0.82%. Active savers and AUM at month 60 equal.
